title: How to Work in Singapore: A Practical Guide for Beginners
summary: Want to know how to work in Singapore? This practical guide covers visas, job hunting, costs, and tips to land your dream job in the Lion City.
body_markdown:
[Singapore](https://blog.transfez.com/en/living-abroad/singapore/)


Singapore is one of those cities that just pulls people in. The skyline is stunning, the food scene is incredible, and the salaries? Let’s just say they have a way of making your eyes widen. If you’ve been daydreaming about building a career in the Lion City, you’re definitely not alone. Thousands of people from all over the world pack their bags every year and head there for exactly that reason.


But here’s the honest truth: figuring out **how to work in Singapore** can feel overwhelming at first. Which visa do you need? How do you even find a job? What does life actually cost over there? Relax. This guide breaks it all down in plain, simple language so you can go in prepared and confident. And if you’re still deciding whether it’s worth the leap, a quick read on[why Singapore is such a popular destination](https://blog.transfez.com/en/why-study-in-singapore/) might help you make up your mind.

##


**Why Singapore Is Worth the Move**


Before diving into the how, let’s talk about the why for a moment. Singapore consistently ranks among the world’s top business hubs. It has a low crime rate, excellent public transport, world-class healthcare, and a multicultural environment where English is widely spoken. For professionals from Southeast Asia and beyond, it offers a quality of life that’s hard to match in the region.


###


**1. A Thriving Job Market Across Many Industries**


Singapore’s economy is diverse and resilient. You’ll find strong demand in sectors like finance, tech, engineering, healthcare, logistics, and professional services. Whether you’re a fresh graduate or a seasoned professional, there’s likely a space for you here.


###


**2. English as the Main Business Language**


One of the biggest advantages for international job seekers is that English is the primary language of business in Singapore. You won’t need to pass a language test or worry about getting lost in translation during meetings.


###


**3. A Gateway to the Rest of Asia**


Working in Singapore often opens doors to regional roles. Many global companies use Singapore as their Asia-Pacific headquarters, which means your career can grow well beyond the island itself.


##


**Understanding Singapore Work Visas**


This is where most people get stuck, so let’s clear it up. Singapore has several types of work passes depending on your qualifications and the type of work you’ll be doing. Getting the right one is the most important step in the whole process.


###


**1. Employment Pass (EP)**


The *Employment Pass* is designed for foreign professionals, managers, and executives. To qualify, you generally need a degree from a recognized university and a job offer from a Singapore-registered company. Your employer applies for this pass on your behalf through Singapore’s Ministry of Manpower (MOM). You don’t apply for it yourself.


###


**2. S Pass**


The *S Pass* is for mid-skilled workers in technical and specialist roles. The salary and qualification requirements are lower than the EP. Again, your employer handles the application. Companies are also subject to a quota on how many S Pass holders they can employ, so competition for these spots can be tight.


###


**3. Personalised Employment Pass (PEP)**


Already an existing EP holder or a high-earning overseas professional? The *Personalised Employment Pass* gives you more flexibility. You can switch jobs without needing to cancel and reapply for a new pass, which is a big deal if you like having career freedom.


###


**4. EntrePass**


Thinking of starting your own business in Singapore instead of joining one? The *EntrePass* is meant for entrepreneurs who want to set up and run a company there. You’ll need to show that your business idea is innovative and has real growth potential.


##


**How to Find a Job in Singapore**


Landing a job in Singapore as a foreigner takes effort, but it’s absolutely doable with the right approach. The key is to be strategic and persistent. Here’s how to go about it.


###


**1. Use the Right Job Portals**


Singapore has several popular job platforms where most legitimate listings are posted. JobStreet, LinkedIn, MyCareersFuture (run by the government), and Indeed Singapore are great starting points. For professional roles, LinkedIn is especially powerful because you can connect directly with hiring managers and recruiters.


###


**2. Tailor Your Resume and LinkedIn Profile**


Singapore employers appreciate clear, concise CVs. Keep yours to two pages max. Highlight measurable achievements, not just job responsibilities. And make sure your LinkedIn profile is complete and up to date because recruiters there are very active on the platform. If you need more tips on the whole job search process, check out this[practical guide on finding a job abroad](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-find-a-job-abroad/) .


###


**3. Network Actively**


In Singapore, who you know genuinely matters. Attend industry events, join professional associations, and connect with alumni networks. Many roles are filled through referrals before they even get publicly posted. If you’re still overseas, online networking via LinkedIn is your best tool.


###


**4. Work with Recruitment Agencies**


Specialist recruiters in Singapore can save you a lot of time. Agencies like Robert Walters, Michael Page, and Hays all have a strong presence there and often work with top employers. They can match your profile to roles you might not find on your own.


###


**5. Apply Early and Follow Up**


Competition is real, so don’t wait around. Apply as soon as a role opens, and send a polite follow-up email if you haven’t heard back within a week or two. Showing genuine interest can help you stand out from the pile.


##


**Preparing for Life in Singapore**


Getting the job is one thing. Actually thriving once you’re there is another. Here are a few things to sort out before or right after you arrive.


###


**1. Sort Out Your Accommodation Early**


Housing in Singapore can be expensive, especially in central areas. Look into HDB flats (government public housing, which many expats rent), condominiums, and co-living spaces. Websites like PropertyGuru and 99.co are popular for browsing listings. The earlier you start searching, the better your options.


###


**2. Open a Local Bank Account**


You’ll want a Singapore bank account as soon as possible for receiving your salary and managing daily expenses. DBS, OCBC, and UOB are the three main local banks. Most require your work pass and proof of address to get started. For a step-by-step walkthrough of the process, this guide on[how to open a bank account abroad](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-open-a-bank-account-abroad/) is really useful.


###


**3. Register with MOM After Arrival**


Once you land and start work, some passes require you to complete in-person registration with Singapore’s Ministry of Manpower within a set period. Your employer should guide you through this, but don’t leave it to the last minute.


###


**4. Understand the Cost of Living**


Singapore is not cheap, but it’s manageable if you plan well. Transport via the MRT and buses is efficient and affordable. Eating at hawker centres keeps food costs low. The bigger expenses tend to be rent and childcare if you’re bringing family along. Budget carefully before you make the move.


###


**5. Send Money Home Without the Hassle**


If you’re supporting family back home, you’ll want a reliable and affordable way to send money internationally. Apps like Transfez make international remittances straightforward, letting you transfer funds from Singapore to Indonesia and other countries with ease. It’s something worth setting up early so your family gets their support on time, every time.

Working in Singapore is a genuinely rewarding experience for those who come prepared. The city rewards hard work, welcomes talent from around the world, and offers a lifestyle that’s hard to find elsewhere in the region. Do your research, get your paperwork right, and put yourself out there. Your Singapore chapter could be closer than you think.
